articleTitle: Game-Theoretic-Based Resource Allocation Algorithm for SCMA Max-Min Problem to Maximize Fairness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper tackles a joint optimization problem in uplink sparse code multiple access (SCMA) networks to enhance network fairness, i.e., Jain's fairness index (JFI). We propose a novel game-theoretic approach, the worst-case player first-strategy selection (WCPFSS) algorithm, to maximize the minimum achievable rate for all subcarriers while ensuring fair power allocation and optimized subcarrier assignment. This approach effectively manages user interference because each subcarrier acts as a player to exchange their strategies, which are clusters of users associated with each subcarrier. The simulation results confirm the superiority of the proposed WCPFSS method w.r.t. JFI for differential setup parameters.

articleTitle: A Ceramic Monoblock Open-Ended Dielectric Waveguide Antenna Array for 5G Millimeter-Wave Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a ceramic monoblock open-ended dielectric waveguide antenna (OEDWA) array operating in the 5G millimeter-wave band is designed. Array element comprises two parts: a feeding section and a ceramic monoblock section. The feeding section is a coaxialline-to-TEM horn, and the TEM horn antenna is plated with gold on the surface of the dielectric to achieve miniaturization. The beams on both sides of the horn have little impact on the radiation performance, and can fix the array element on the metal plate. The OEDWA and the two beams are made of the same dielectric material, therefore, they can be integrally designed. The ceramic monoblock section is excited by a TEM horn antenna through a low dielectric constant dielectric waveguide (DW), forming OEDWA, which matching the radiating section with the air directly. In addition, OEDWA is an excellent array element with broadband matching, low sidelobe levels, and high directionality. DWs transmit in the form of surface waves, achieving high isolation between array elements. The n-element linear array ceramic monoblock can be designed by fixing it to the bottom plate. And then, the large-scale antenna array is composed of m rows of n-element linear array elements. Finally, a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${2}\times {2}$</tex> array is selected as a validation example, which has a matching bandwidth from 24 to 26GHz with the voltage standing wave rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({VSWR}) \leq {2}$</tex> and the realized gain ranges from 15.7 to 16.5dBi.

articleTitle: A Low-PAPR VLC System Based on Adaptively Biased Optical OFDM and Tone Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Adaptively biased optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (ABO-OFDM), as a new type of optical orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (O-OFDM) transmission method, has the advantage of low receiver complexity, high subcarrier utilization and power utilization rate. However, ABO-OFDM signals have the drawback of high peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR). In this paper, we propose a novel low PAPR ABO-OFDM (LP-ABO-OFDM) visible light communication system based on the idea of tone injection (TI) technique to achieve a better PAPR performance. The LP-ABO-OFDM method achieves a PAPR reduction of up to approximately 3.5 dB while addressing the issue of traditional TI strategies being inapplicable to ABO-OFDM. Simulation results have shown that the PAPR of the signal with the proposed LP-ABO-OFDM is significantly lower compared to traditional O-OFDM signals, and the BER under simulated nonlinear device distortion conditions is significantly lower than that of the traditional O-OFDM signal.

articleTitle: Filter Design Based on a New Tiered Circuit Board Process Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, two filters are designed based on tiered circuit board (TCB) process transmission lines. The first filter is a low-pass filter with a cutoff frequency of 23 GHz. It exhibits an in-band return loss of less than −20 dB and an insertion loss of less than 0.2 dB, achieving an out-of-band suppression of 30 dB at 25 GHz. The second filter is a band-pass filter with an operational bandwidth ranging from 10.8 GHz to 12.4 GHz. It demonstrates an in-band return loss of less than −24 dB and an insertion loss of less than 0.2 dB, with out-of-band suppression exceeding 30 dB below 9.5 GHz and above 15 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Influence of Dielectric Coating on Transmission Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The breakdown of air discharge on the antenna surface can cause structural damage, which is the main factor affecting the antenna power capacity. In this paper, the surface of the transmission metasurface and transmission array antenna are coated with polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) to convert the air discharge breakdown into dielectric breakdown, reduce the electric field intensity of the antenna, and increase the power capacity. After coating PTFE dielectric material with thickness of 2mm, the surface electric field intensity of the transmission metasurface decreases from 296.17V/cm to 153.67V/cm. The surface electric field intensity of the antenna array decreases from 25.73V/cm to 16.67V/cm, and the gain increases from 21.80dB to 23.10dB. It can be proved that coating dielectric material on the antenna surface can reduce the electric field intensity and increase the power capacity of the antenna.

articleTitle: A Wideband Frequency Division Duplex High Temperature Resistant Antenna Based on Open-Ended Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband frequency division duplex (FDD) high temperature resistant open-ended waveguide antenna with wide beam performance is designed. The antenna uses two coaxial probes to feed vertically at adjacent sides of the open-ended waveguide, enabling the antenna to achieve high isolation duplex communication with perpendicular polarization directions in different frequency bands. At the same time, the open-ended waveguide antenna with a metal floor is placed under thermal insulation material to realize high temperature resistance performance. The thermal protection shield is fixed to the metal floor through screws and filled with thermal insulation material. The simulation results show that the FDD high-temperature resistant antenna can achieve wide beam radiation from 3.5GHz to 4.5 GHz and 7GHz to 9 GHz, respectively. Under the continuous temperature of 1200°C for 2000s, the temperature at two feed ports is kept below 150°C.

articleTitle: A Differential-Fed Dual-Polarized Antenna with Air Backed Cavity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a differential-fed dual-polarized antenna with air backed cavity is proposed for Ku-band applications. Two pairs of T-shaped probes are used to feed the radiation patch to form orthogonal dual-polarized waves, and shunt open stubs are added to the T-shaped probes to effectively expand the operation bandwidth. The simulation results demonstrate that the return loss is less than -15.0 dB in the frequency band of 13 GHz~15 GHz, the port isolation is less than -30.0 dB, and the cross-polarization ratio is greater than 30.0 dB.

articleTitle: YOLOv8 Based Vehicle Object Detection Using Two-Stage Multi-Modality Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In response to the issue of degraded detection performance of vehicle targets in autonomous driving scenarios due to varying degrees of occlusion and scale changes, this paper proposes a robust decision-level multimodal fusion object detection method. Firstly, natural images captured by camera, sparse depth maps (DM) and bird's eye view maps (BEVM) generated from the LiDAR point cloud information are separately fed into the end-to-end object detector YOLOv8. The employed YOLOv8 incorporates improved regression losses via Wise-IOU loss, for target position regression and classification within their respective modalities. Secondly, to address the problem of poor detection performance for heavily occluded targets, a K-nearest neighbor multi-output regressor (MOR) algorithm is used to transform BEV detection boxes into the frontal view. A two-stage fusion approach based on soft non-maximum suppression (soft-NMS) is adopted to fuse detection results from the three modalities (natural images, DM and BEVM). The first fusion is conducted by combining results from color images and DM, and the result is further fused with the transformed BEV detection results. The experimental results on the KITTI dataset demonstrate that the proposed method exhibits comprehensive advantages in both detection accuracy and speed compared to various other detection methods and specifically improves the detection performance for heavily occluded targets.

articleTitle: Widely Memory-Canonical Piecewise Linear-Based Self-Interference Canceller for Full-Duplex Radios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a widely memory-canonical piecewise linear (WMCPWL)-based model for the digital self-interference cancellation (DSIC) in In-band full-duplex communication systems is proposed. Unlike previous polynomial-based and neural networks (NN)-based models, the proposed one decomposes the total self-interference (SI) signals into widely linear and WMCPWL components, the latter of which is introduced to mimic the nonlinearity and memory effects between transmitting and receiving paths. Moreover, the image rejection ratio (IRR) which generally quantifies the IQ imbalance can be extracted by estimating SI channel coefficients corresponding to the widely linear part. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model decreases both computational complexities and model parameters while providing a similar cancellation performance compared with other state-of-the-art models.

articleTitle: A Miniaturized Half TEM Horn Antenna for UWB Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, a miniaturized half transverse electromagnetic (TEM) horn antenna is designed for ultra-wideband (UWB) wireless communication. Two radiation modes are generally utilized to extend the impedance bandwidth of traditional TEM horn antennas: one is the combined magneto-electric dipole mode at low frequencies, the other is the TEM horn mode. However, the size of the antenna is relatively big, so the miniaturization is realized by replacing half of the antenna structure with a ground plate to form a half TEM horn antenna. A trapezoidal plate is added to compensate for the magnetic dipoles destroyed by the ground plates to extend the low frequency band while the exponential tapered ridge is used to obtain better impedance match. Besides, an upper ridge contributes to stronger mechanical property. The final configuration whose electrical size is only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${0.6} {\lambda}_{{L}} \ast {0.36} {\lambda}_{{L}} \ast {0.34} {\lambda}_{{L}} ({\lambda}_{{L}}$</tex> being the free-space wavelength at the lowest frequency) is compact and stable enough to be manufactured integrally. The designed antenna has a broad bandwidth from 3 to 12 GHz with the voltage standing wave rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$({VSWR}) \leq {2.5}$</tex> and the gain ranges from 4.6 to 9.5dBi.

articleTitle: Mutual Coupling Reduction for Linearly and Circularly Polarized Electromagnetic Wave Based on Miniaturized Absorptive Metamaterial
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this paper, an absorptive metamaterial unit cell consisting of a round microstrip line with four lumped elements loaded at the midpoint of each side is proposed. This unit cell, exhibiting central symmetry and being polarization-insensitive to incident waves, is ideally suited for capturing circularly polarized waves within its resonance frequency band. In contrast to the majority of previous research that focused on large-scale metamaterial structures, this paper introduces a novel approach aimed at miniaturizing the metamaterial while preserving its exceptional absorption characteristics. By simplifying the periodic boundary of the metamaterial cell unit, a one-dimensional absorptive metamaterial comprising merely four unit cells is introduced between two closely spaced microstrip antennas. A comprehensive numerical analysis is conducted, examining the coupling coefficient, impedance matching, and radiation characteristics under both linearly and circularly polarized scenarios. The simulation results reveal that the presence of this absorptive metamaterial effectively suppresses mutual coupling by over 27 dB, while simultaneously enhancing impedance matching and optimizing the axial ratio (AR).

articleTitle: Wide-Range and High-Precision Doppler Simulation for Inter-Satellite Coherent Optical Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Coherent free-space optical communication has emerged as a critical technology for high-speed data transmission between satellites. However, the significant relative velocities between satellites result in substantial Doppler shifts, making signal synchronization and demodulation challenging. A Doppler simulation method based on changing the signal clock frequency is proposed. This method reproduces the Doppler effect caused by relative motion during satellite operations, enabling the verification of Doppler tracking and compensating algorithms. The proposed method allows for the flexible generation of Doppler shifts based on satellite orbit information. The designed hardware platform allows for a performed Doppler range of [-20, 20] km/s and a simulation accuracy of 1.8 × 10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>m/s, encompassing the Doppler between various orbital altitudes.

articleTitle: Error Detection and Correction Codes for Memories with Enhanced Detection Abilities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Recent memories in different processors suffer from increasing threats of errors. Error correction and detection codes with higher detection abilities are required. This work presents the design and implement of error control abilities of codes in different data lengths, realizing burst error correction abilities from 1 bit to 4 bits, detection abilities of 3-bit random errors and detection abilities of over 5 bits burst errors. Lower hardware overhead is realized for error detection. The proposed codes can be adopted to improve reliability of memories when increasing bits of burst errors and random errors need correcting and recovering.

articleTitle: TransVNet: A Network to Improve TransUNet Using VGG16
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The method based on Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) can automatically and accurately segment objects in medical images. The combination of CNN and long-range dependency feature extraction techniques, such as TransUNet, can further improve segmentation performance. However, the segmentation performance of TransUNet is affected by the feature extraction ability of the CNN architecture. In order to improve the liver segmentation performance of TransUNet in abdominal CT images, this paper proposes a TransVNet architecture that combines CNN and Transformer using a symmetrical U-shaped architecture, and uses skip connections to connect features between corresponding convolution stages. To verify the effectiveness of TransVNet in segmenting the liver in abdominal CT, we compared its performance with other liver segmentation methods using 5-fold cross validation on the public dataset 3Dircadb. The experimental results show that the proposed architecture achieves the highest average DICE score of 95.29%.

articleTitle: Color-Based Ripeness Classification of Oil Palm Fresh Fruit Bunches Using Convolution Neural Networks and Data Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Proper ripeness categorization of oil palm fresh fruit bunches is essential to ensure they are harvested at the optimal stage to maximize oil output. The current manual method of ripeness assessment, which relies on harvesters visually inspecting the fruit's color, is both labor-intensive and prone to human error. To address these limitations, there is a growing need for an automated classification system that leverages artificial intelligence. The manual classification process is cumbersome and susceptible to inaccuracies due to its reliance on subjective visual inspection. This labor-intensive approach increases the likelihood of human error, underscoring the necessity for a more reliable and efficient automated solution. Thus, this study aims to evaluate the feasibility of using Convolutional Neural Networks for automating the grading based on color. A dataset was compiled from various sources and augmented using a data generator. The model was constructed incorporating a transfer learning approach with an Xception model. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 80.4%. Visualization of the model using activation maps confirmed that the model can effectively classify the color, indicating its potential viability for the task.

articleTitle: Research on Synchronization Problem of Triple Redundancy Flight Control Computer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: This paper introduces an integral data balancing algorithm using dual-port RAM as the hardware medium. Its aim is to address the issue of inconsistent integral data between master and slave controls due to clock errors in the operation of a three-redundant flight control computer. We first propose a three-redundant flight control computer architecture based on comparative monitoring, and we design the software and hardware to support subsequent semi-physical simulations. The data balancing algorithm primarily targets integral data by exchanging the integrator output values among the three main branches to achieve signal balance. The monitoring branch then transmits the balanced integral values to the main branch, ensuring consistency between the master and slave controls. Simulation verification demonstrates that this data balancing algorithm effectively resolves the issue of inconsistent integral data under both synchronous and asynchronous conditions, thereby enhancing the reliability of the flight control computer.

articleTitle: A Nature-Inspired Energy-Efficient Clustering Protocol Based on Improved Hybrid Grey Wolf Optimization for FANETs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Flying ad hoc networks (FANETs) are composed of multiple UA V nodes that are distributed across a wide area and linked via wireless communication to gather and transmit environmental data. However, the battery-powered UAVs in FANETs imposes significant energy limitations, thereby shortening the network's operational lifespan. This paper proposes an energy-efficient clustering protocol based on improved hybrid grey wolf optimization (EEC-IHGWO), which can optimally select cluster heads (CHs), significantly extend network lifetime and maximize energy efficiency. The selection criteria include factors like remaining energy, the distance from cluster members to CHs, and node density. The performance of the EEC-IHGWO method, measured by network lifetime, the number of living nodes, and remaining energy, is assessed against traditional algorithms such as LEACH, as well as the more recent PSO and FCM. The simulation results demonstrate that EEC-IHGWO sustains a longer network lifetime and higher energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Robust Augmented Diffusion Active Noise Control Algorithm Based on Generalized Maximum Correntropy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Multichannel active noise control (ANC) is a noise cancellation technology designed to effectively eliminate low-frequency noise, thereby creating a large quiet zone in a given space. Distributed ANC systems based on diffusion strategies have garnered significant attention due to their low computational complexity and flexible scalability. However, recent related works have largely overlooked the interference of impulsive noise on these systems, developing algorithms solely based on the mean square error (MSE) criterion. This paper addresses this gap by employing the generalized maximum correntropy criterion (GMCC) and introducing an augmented weight vector for the control filter. Consequently, we develop an augmented diffusion filtered-x GMCC (ADFxGMCC) algorithm. Finally, computer simulations validate the robust noise reduction performance of the proposed algorithm in asymmetric ANC systems under impulsive noise interference.

articleTitle: Precise Interaction Integrating Stereopsis and Gesture Detected by Binocular Depth-Camera
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: How to precisely integrate stereopsis and gesture is widely studied in recently years <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[1]–[4]</sup>. To deeply conduct researches on direct interaction and be different from other researches, we develop a directly interactive system integrating stereopsis and binocular gestural detection, and present an improved interactive algorithm in this paper. Compared with the TOF depth-camera and the traditional interactive algorithm, the binocular depth-camera can generate a more precise gestural detection, and the improved interactive algorithm can integrate the stereopsis system and the gestural system better. The experimental result for operating the system and completing the interaction demonstrates that the developed system and the presented algorithm can obtain a higher interactive precision.

articleTitle: Enhanced Channel Estimation for 6G Urban V2V Communication Using BPNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: With the sixth generation (6G) era approaching, the Internet of Vehicles (Io V) has attracted much attention as a key application. The future Vehicle-to-Vehicle (V2V) communication in 6G urban scenarios has a larger data volume, which requires faster data rate, lower latency, and more reliable communication quality. To meet these requirements, this paper conducts channel modeling for 6G urban V2V communication scenarios and proposes a channel estimator based on a three-layer back-propagation neural network (BPNN), where each BPNN estimates the channel response at a single frequency point. Simulation results show that the performance of BPNN in 6G urban environment is better than that of traditional channel estimation algorithm.

articleTitle: Data Throughput Maximization in a Novel Hybrid TDMA-NOMA System Based on Time Allocation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: By 2030, the number of mobile IoT connections in China will reach a scale of billions. Therefore, efficiently transmitting more data within limited time and resources has become an urgent problem to address. In this paper, we consider a novel hybrid non-orthogonal multiple access (NH-NOMA) system based on downlink transmission links with opportunistic time allocation. We develop a new hybrid non-orthogonal multiple access model based on time allocation, where the data transmitted by users in different time slots is rederived. To maximize the system's data transmission while meeting the users' data requirements, we approximate the non-convex problem as a convex optimization problem to approach the optimal solution. Finally, simulation results demonstrated that a time allocation based hybrid multiple access system achieves higher data transmission efficiency compared to traditional orthogonal multiple access systems and time division-based hybrid systems. This system effectively utilizes users with favorable channel conditions to maximize their data transmission while ensuring the basic communication needs of other users.

articleTitle: Vertical Transition of Transmission Lines Based on Tiered Circuit Boards Process
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In this work, two low-loss vertical transitions are presented for tiered circuit board transmission line. The first configuration achieves strong coupling between two opposite tiered circuit board transmission lines by etching a rectangular slot in the ground plane. Simulation results demonstrate that the vertical transition has a reflection coefficient better than 25 dB from 28 GHz to 32 GHz, and an insertion loss of about 0.2 dB. The second configuration connects the upper and lower TCB TLs directly by means of slopes and mortise-tenon structure. Simulation results exhibit that the vertical transition has a reflection coefficient better than 28 dB and an insertion loss of about 0.2 dB from 10 to 32 GHz. This configuration is characterized by ultra-broadband.

articleTitle: NetOps-VL: Leveraging Multimodal LLM for Enhanced Network Operations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Multimodal large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated powerful abilities in interpreting various common image scenarios, attributed to their extensive parameters and varied datasets. However, in specific domains like Network Operations (NetOps), their effectiveness is limited by insufficient knowledge about network equipment features, stemming from a lack of domain-specific expertise. Meanwhile, small visual models with convolutional layers, despite having fewer parameters and faster inference speeds, often require separate training for each NetOps visual task, and their cost may not always be lower than that of general LLMs. To tackle this challenge, we constructed a Visual Question Answering (VQA) dataset focused on image recognition and OCR tasks for network infrastructure within the NetOps domain. Subsequently, we employed GPT-4 as a teacher model to generate Chain of Thought (CoT) prompts, and utilized the created dataset to fine-tune the original multimodal LLM. This approach ensures that the enhanced multimodal LLM attains proficiency in NetOps domain knowledge. We propose the method for generating CoT prompts as “multimodal fine-tune-CoT”. The fine-tuned LLMs is referred to as NetOps-VL. In our experiments, we conducted multiple tests to validate multimodal fine-tune-CoT's effectiveness. The results indicate that NetOps-VL exhibits some advantages over other methods on the test dataset. Moreover, NetOps-VL improves NetOps image and text comprehension without sacrificing its general visual capabilities.

articleTitle: Stability Investigation in Tellurium Field-Effect Transistors Grown via Hydrothermal Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Negative Bias Temperature Instability (NBTI) remains a critical concern affecting the reliability of field-effect transistors (FETs). Quasi-2D Tellurium (Te) emerges as a promising p-type alternative for high-performance FETs due to its high hole mobility and excellent air stability. In this study, FETs based on quasi-2D Te grown via the hydrothermal method were fabricated, and the NBTI effect was investigated under various conditions of negative bias stress, temperature, and stress duration. The power-law time-exponents (n) extracted at 300 K closely approximates 0.5, indicating the diffusing species as H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>. Furthermore, an elucidation of the interaction effects involving water/oxygen, Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>ions, H<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>ions, and internal traps sheds light on the plausible mechanism underlying the observed current degradation due to NBTI. Then the low-frequency noise (LFN) dominant model as ▵N model is determined. Finally, the interface traps number of 1.96×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>eV<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>is extracted.

articleTitle: Local Power Control and Precoding in Cell-Free Massive MIMO Systems with Distributed Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) has garnered significant attention due to its ability on reducing the path loss and providing uniform service quality. As the cell boundary eliminates, the inter-user interference is dominant. Hence, power control and precoding which can effectively surpass the inter-user interference become crucial in CF-mMIMO. However, the practical application of them needs centralized information on the central processing unit which leads to challenges from the fronthaul payload and delays constraints. To address this issue, we propose a distributed learning (DL) framework to design local power control and precoding. Specifically, we deploy distributed deep neural network (DNN) models at each access point, which takes the optimal max-min power control as the label to train the local power control, and take the centralized zero-forcing precoding as label to train a local precoding. This approach do not need channel state information exchange during the entire process, resulting in a CF-mMIMO system with fully local signal processing. The simulation results show that the DL-aided power control and precoding can significantly improve the spectral efficiency over the existing local methods. Its advantage is more pronounced for a larger scale of CF-mMIMO.

articleTitle: Multi-User Scheduling Based on Improved CNN for Massive MIMO Industrial IoT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The rapid development of the 5th Generation Mobile System (5G) brings many challenges. Since the number of nodes in the Internet of Things (IoT) system, 5G adopts millimeter wave and massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) technology. Due to the large number of IoT nodes, a substantial computational load will be generated in the massive MIMO system when applying the traditional multi-user scheduling algorithms. In this paper, a multi-user scheduling algorithm based on the improved Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) is proposed. This algorithm uses the predictive characteristics of the neural network to calculate the channel capacity. The improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO) algorithm is used to find the optimal network structure parameters of the CNN to acquire the CNN with high prediction accuracy and achieve low computational complexity in the scenario with massive users accessed.

articleTitle: Trajectory and Phase Shift Design for Maritime UAV-ARIS System Based on Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: In maritime wireless communication networks, the link between unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) temporary base stations and buoy sensors may be obstructed by passing ships and small islands et al, which lead to reduce or interrupt data transmission rates. To address this problem, this paper introduces an aerial reconfigurable intelligent surface (ARIS) to assist maritime UA V communication systems. In our study, we are considering the use of deep reinforcement learning algorithm DDQN to simultaneously optimize the 3D trajectory of the UA V and the passive reflection phase shift of ARIS to enhance the UA V ‘sdata transmission rate and reduce its overall Energy Consumption (EC), ultimately maximizing the UA V's Energy Efficiency (EE). Extensive simulation results demonstrate that with the assistance of DDQN algorithms, the EE of the maritime UA V communication system with optimal ARIS phase shift assistance surpasses that of systems with random ARIS phase shift assistance or without ARIS assistance.

articleTitle: A Temporal Data Compression Based on Dual Autoregressive Prediction Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: A temporal data compression method based on rebuilding the predictive model is proposed. This method employs a dual autoregressive prediction model to forecast the temporal data, storing only the residuals between the predicted and actual values, along with the coefficients of the prediction model. During decoding, the prediction model coefficients are used to reconstruct the prediction model to generate predicted values, which are then combined with the residuals to recover the original values. Since the residuals are significantly smaller than the original values, they can be quantized using fewer bits, while the prediction model coefficients, once stored, do not need to be stored repeatedly over time.Experimental results on eight real datasets of varying sizes and types demonstrate the excellent compression performance of this method.

articleTitle: Computational Energy Efficiency Optimization for IRS-Assisted MEC System: Active or Passive?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Active intelligent reflecting surfaces (AIRS) effectively overcome the multiplicative path loss effects encountered by passive intelligent reflecting surfaces (PIRS). To unleash the full potential of MEC systems, this paper investigates AIRS-assisted MEC systems in a multi-user scenario. Enhancing energy efficiency has emerged as a primary goal of 6G networks. Although AIRS has been shown to greatly improve the computational rate of MEC systems, its impact on computational energy efficiency (CEE) has not been fully studied. Therefore, this study aims to maximize CEE as the optimization objective, posing a challenging non-convex fractional programming (FP) problem. To address this issue, we propose an iterative algorithm based on the Dinkel-bach method. We first transform the initial problem into a convex optimization problem using the FP method. We then employ the block coordinate descent (BCD) method to decouple the reformulated problem and derive closed-form optimal solutions for each subproblem through Lagrangian dual transformation and KKT conditions. Simulation results validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, and elucidate the preferable operating points for choosing between AIRS and PIRS in terms of CEE.

articleTitle: Robust Secure Hybrid Beamforming for RSMA Integrated Sensing and Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Sharing resources in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems poses a serious threat to the security of users information. In this paper, we consider the rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) ISAC system based on the partially-connected hybrid beamforming architecture, where the target is a potential eavesdropper. To improve the performance of sensing and secure communication, we provide a robust hybrid beamforming scheme. Specially, we derive performance metrics for sensing and secure communication under the target location uncertainty. Then we formulate the sensing performance optimization problem meanwhile satisfying the secure communication, hardware and power constraints. To address the intractability of this non-convex problem, we propose a suboptimal iterative algorithm relying on semidefinite relaxation (SDR) and inner majorization-minimization (iMM) to alternately design digital and analog beamformers. Simulation results show the outperformance of the proposed approach over the existing hybrid beamformer design based on Eucliden distance in guaranteeing secure communication and sensing.

articleTitle: Accurate Detection of Heart Disease Using the CardioFusion Ensemble Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to use Artificial Intelligence approaches to create an effective and precise diagnostic tool to detect heart disease problem. Heart disease is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. We compared AI techniques to diagnose heart disease, such as Deep Learning, Multi-layer Perceptron, Random Forest, Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting, Radial SVM, Linear SVM, AdaBoost, Linear SVM, Logistic Regression, and K-Nearest Neighbor. By identifying important predictors feature selection techniques like sigmoid and Rectified Linear Unit, were used to improve model accuracy. Our algorithm showed better accuracy, sensitivity, and specificity: mostly, Random Forest classifiers superior performance metrics is evidenced by their 98% accuracy rate. This underscores the significance of incorporating these technologies into healthcare systems to improve patient outcomes and lower the prevalence of heart disease. Our research shows the MLP-GA algorithm can increase diagnostic accuracy.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Secure Communications for Metaverse Library Cross-Border Payments: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: The metaverse library is a kind of virtual library that can be accessed by users throughout the world. While cross-border payments represent the globalization of trade and finance and are regarded as a powerful tool for promoting financial inclusion, it is important to focus on the security issues of cross-border payments in metaverse libraries. Ripple incorporates blockchain technology into the XRP Ledger to enhance the efficiency of funds transfers. The purpose of this report is to explore the issues of the current metaverse library cross-border payment systems and evaluate the usefulness of XRP in comparison to the Society for Worldwide Interbank Financial Telecommunication (SWIFT), the current most popular inter-bank fund transfer system. This paper concludes that traditional metaverse library cross-border payments lack a streamlined, automated, and transparent system, which XRP could tackle through its high scalability, interoperability, and sound mechanisms. Nevertheless, due to concerns over decentralization and regulatory challenges, further development is needed for XRP to truly revolutionize the field. Taking the metaverse library as an application instance, this paper reviews the traditional and modern cross-border payments based on blockchains. Secure communication techniques are focused. Possible future research directions about secure communications in metaverse libraries are also presented.

articleTitle: Substation Alarm Association Method Based on ATT&CK Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of island, fragmentation and redundancy of smart substation alarm information, this paper proposes a substation alarm correlation method based on ATT&CK framework by introducing ATT&CK threat intelligence, which is used to correlate and fuse the alarm information in the smart substation station to improve the efficiency of security protection. The method describes the attack technique by constructing semantic rule model and generating semantic rule graph. Then, a semantic rule extraction framework is constructed to extract knowledge from ATT&CK framework's attack technology text, from which semantic rules are extracted, covering 14 attack tactics and 244 attack technologies of ATT&CK framework, to realize automatic analysis and processing of high-level threat intelligence. Finally, the proposed method is tested in the simulation environment of simulated intelligent substation, and compared with the current mainstream IOC indicators to test the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Optimizing Cache Management Policy for Fast Packet Processing in NFV Data Plane
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Establishing efficient caching in the data plane is crucial for the performance of packet forwarding for network function virtualization(NFV). For switches that provide network functions such as forwarding, routing, and firewall, the on-chip memory in the data plane is closest to the packet processing logic. However, due to hardware constraints or limitations in the programming model, the programmability and memory access capabilities of data plane caching in many network devices, such as programmable switches, smart network cards, and DPUs, are often restricted. As a result, most existing data plane caches rely on simple and inefficient replacement strategies. In this paper, an analysis of the limitations in programmability of the data plane is conducted, and an algorithm with bit-slice operators is proposed to determine the update and eviction strategy for each item in the cache array. Leveraging the principles of limited associativity design, the storage structure of the ternary match kind identifier (TCAM) table is optimized due to constraints on the number of mask bits. Efficient utilization of cache hits is achieved by setting timestamps and packet flow identifiers in registers. Experimental results demonstrate that our caching strategy exhibits significant improvements in hit rate and latency performance compared to some previously proposed approaches.

articleTitle: Virtual Topology Based Hierarchical Networking for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Swarm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Conference on Electronics and Communication Engineering (ICECE)
abstract: Flying Ad-hoc Networks (FANETs) consisting of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) are challenged by its disorder and time-varying topology, diverse link conditions, large network scale, etc. The existing networking algorithms designed for FANETs are limited by high networking overheads and low scalability. To tackle these shortages, a hierarchical partitioned network architecture for Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms is proposed, which reduces the complexity of network hierarchy and enhances fault tolerance in UAV swarm networks. To achieve hierarchical networking, a weight-based cluster head election and update mechanism is established, which induces adjustable parameters related to node communication ranges to facilitate flexible adjustment and restructuring of the network topology, thereby enhancing network longevity. Moreover, we propose a hierarchical networking algorithm based on virtual topology for efficient networking of UAV swarms. This algorithm constructs a two-layer virtual topology consisting of a main route and several branch routes based on virtual identifiers. This results in a distributed FANET with high degrees of freedom and reconfigurability, facilitating communication and coordination among UAV nodes at different layers. Simulation results show that compared with the existing virtual topology-based networking algorithm and the enhanced MPR selection algorithm, the proposed algorithm provides better performance in terms of signaling overhead and network convergence time.
